### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**14** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **4** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **18** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 199e3624426faa50f413e18657abc44ea20ff3cb` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `062d1e3016653c2e6a6ca3ec573b1b9fc0bdbc32` — the merge of head `428a74261b9955d95fcd3908374dd3f253f8f30f` into base `199e3624426faa50f413e18657abc44ea20ff3cb`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 062d1e3016653c2e6a6ca3ec573b1b9fc0bdbc32 && git checkout 062d1e3016653c2e6a6ca3ec573b1b9fc0bdbc32
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 199e3624426faa50f413e18657abc44ea20ff3cb 428a74261b9955d95fcd3908374dd3f253f8f30f && git checkout -B drift-repro 199e3624426faa50f413e18657abc44ea20ff3cb && git merge --no-ff 428a74261b9955d95fcd3908374dd3f253f8f30f

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 199e3624426faa50f413e18657abc44ea20ff3cb
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `22394872a44138749feb7f6fd5aa9b2b0d908600`
Local-runs: none
Scope: none (no reviewFace hits; the face is the needs:contract-review label alone) + packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/position-renamed-holder-carry.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-start-hooks.ts

Read, not reviewed: ruling A1 (record 6841971722 on #32983) and its conditions, the `metadata:reloaded` announcers on `origin/main`, `packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts`, and `metadata-change-invalidation.ts` and `security-plugin.ts` in plugin-security. The test file, the changeset and the PR prose are the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Published schema and authorable keys: none changed. Right.** No `packages/spec` path; `Metadata-protocol: none` matches.
- **Package public surface: unchanged. Right.** `createPositionRenameCarryRuns`, `PositionRenameCarryRuns` and the new optional parameter of `logPositionRenameCarry` live in a module only `security-plugin-start-hooks.ts` imports; `carryRenamedPositionHoldersAtBoot` keeps its signature.
- **Behavioural accept-set: widened, and wider than the PR states. Wrong as declared.** The system write that changes who holds a position ran at `kernel:bootstrapped` only; it now runs on every `metadata:reloaded` after the boot run, whatever the announcement names. The module doc, the hook comment and the changeset list only some of the doors that announce that event. See ④ finding 1.
- **Hook ordering: right.** `SecurityPlugin` depends on the ObjectQL engine plugin, so its `metadata:reloaded` handler runs after ObjectQL's ingest.
- **Gate verdicts:** 56 check-runs on this head, every one `success` or `skipped`, none failed or pending.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/plugin-security: patch` matches what the diff publishes: a behaviour change inside one plugin, no new export, no schema or authorable key. `Clause-②: no` is on the PR body and the changeset and is right. Check Changeset is `success`.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **open_questions 1 (the ADR-0150 D7 addendum says the carry runs at boot only): escalated, not answered here.** Ruling condition 4 records this system write as one ADR-0150 addendum line; this PR makes that line false the moment it lands. `docs/adr` is Tier H and outside the card's surface, so a separate docs-only PR is the right route, but it is owed with this change. The `PositionSchema.renamedFrom` describe text and the `packages/spec/liveness/position.json` evidence line are in the same state and belong to the same follow-up.
- **open_questions 2 (the runtime `POST /packages` install and enable routes do not announce): answered.** Not this PR; a runtime-lane card of its own, as the dev recommends.
- **`Fixes #33238` overstates what lands: escalated to the lane seat.** The card's headline case is a hot marketplace upgrade; by the dev's own measurement a hot upgrade on this door still carries only at the next restart. The card should stay open (`Part of`), or a follow-up card should carry the upgrade path, before the merge closes it.
- **Out-of-scope finding (a re-register of an installed id withdraws none of the previous version's items): noted;** the lane seat decides whether to file it.
- The dev report's `security_findings: none` does not hold: see ④ finding 1.

### ④ Design judgment

No `hits` file. Both implementing files were read against ruling A1 and its conditions, and against the announcers on `origin/main`.

**Finding 1 — must-fix. Security finding; detail held by review#2.**
- **Where:** `createPositionRenameCarryRuns` (`afterReload`) in `position-renamed-holder-carry.ts`, and the `metadata:reloaded` hook in `security-plugin-start-hooks.ts`.
- **Rule broken:** ruling condition 2 (a package cannot claim an old name it never owned) must hold on the reload path exactly as on the boot path. The reload run as written does not keep it: it ignores what the announcement names and re-judges every claim in the environment on any reload.
- **Required change:** a reload run judges only the renames declared by the package or position the announcement names as registered at that moment, and an announcement of a withdrawal carries nothing.
- **Pin:** condition 2 on the reload path, both ways, through the announcing doors, as the ruling requires of the boot path.
- **Doc:** the "When it runs" section and the hook comment name every announcer the code runs on, and "Its one limit" says what a reload run reads.

**Finding 2 — should-fix.** `afterReload` and `carryRenamedPositionHolders`: once any position declares `renamedFrom` (a standing state; HotCRM declares twelve), every `metadata:reloaded` pays the full read set (catalog list, activation-ledger reads, one holder read per claim, and the left-behind walk over pending `sys_approval_request` and `sys_invitation` rows, even when nothing moved). The publish and install doors await their announce, so each waits for it. The scoping in finding 1 removes this; any unscoped run that remains must skip the left-behind read when no row moved.

**Nits:** the `PositionRenameCarryReport.failed` jsdoc still says only the next boot reads what is left on the old name; `carryRenamedPositionHoldersAtBoot` has no production caller after this diff and its jsdoc could say it is kept for callers and tests; the "What it does" section still opens at `kernel:bootstrapped` with no pointer to "When it runs".

**Held against the design and found sound:** the boot gate (`booted` is set before the boot run is queued, and an earlier reload reads nothing); serialization on one promise chain where a failed run does not poison the next; a catalog reader built per run; dedup by message over the previous run only; the failure path never throws to the announcing door.

A must-fix and a should-fix earn a delta review of their fix by this seat.

Reviewed-by: `session_01FEkQ5nhu4dRbKVQKDB4CDB`

**VERDICT: FAIL**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`

Local-runs: none
Scope: none (no reviewFace hits; the face is the needs:contract-review label alone) + packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/position-renamed-holder-carry.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-start-hooks.ts

Read, not reviewed: ruling A1 (record 6841971722 on #32983) and its conditions; on `origin/main`, the `metadata:reloaded` announcers (the marketplace install-local door, `ObjectQLPlugin.announcePerItemPublish`, the runtime publish-drafts route, `MetadataPlugin._reloadAndAnnounce`) and `SchemaRegistry.getPackage` / `uninstallPackage`. The test file, the changeset and the PR prose are the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`.

### ① Derived judgments

Delta review of round-1 record 6879548824 (FAIL at `22394872`). The delta is commits `6962ec28f7`, `e68ce50b0a` and `428a74261b`; the whole diff was read again at the new head.

Round-1 findings, graded in the tree:

- **Finding 1 (must-fix, condition 2 on the reload path): closed.** `positionRenameReloadScope` reads the scope from the announcement when it arrives: `app/ID` counts only while the registry holds package `ID`; `position/NAME` counts in name grammar; every other entry, and a payload with no list, names nothing. `carryRenamedPositionHolders` with `only` drops every old name no in-scope position claims, before any read or write for it, while the refusals are still judged over the whole catalog, the disabled packages and the ledger. `afterReload` with an empty scope reads nothing and queues no run. The pin is there, on a real kernel through the doors' payload spellings, both ways, and the dev's ablation of the filter line turns only that pin red. "When it runs" and the hook comment name each announcer, and "Its one limit" says what a reload run reads.
- **Finding 2 (should-fix, read cost of every reload): closed.** No unscoped reload run remains; a scoped reload reads the left-behind references only for old names it moved rows of. The boot run is the one unscoped run and is unchanged.
- **Round-1 nits: all three closed.**

Derived judgments at this head:

- **Published schema and authorable keys: none changed. Right.** `Metadata-protocol: none` matches.
- **Package public surface: unchanged. Right.** The new exports live in a module only the start hooks import; the third parameter of `carryRenamedPositionHolders` is optional, so the boot call is the same judgement as before.
- **Behavioural accept-set: widened, and now as declared. Right.** The system write runs at boot over every claim, and after a reload only over the claims of what the announcement names as registered; the module doc, the hook comment, the changeset and the PR body all state that one set.
- **Hook ordering: right.** The scope is read when the announcement arrives, after the announcing door has registered or withdrawn its package; the catalog is read when the run executes.
- **Gate verdicts:** 55 check-runs on this head, 37 `success` and 18 `skipped`, none failed or pending.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/plugin-security: patch` matches what the diff publishes: a behaviour change inside one plugin, no schema or authorable key, no export a consumer reaches. `Clause-②: no` is on the PR body and the changeset and is right. Check Changeset is `success`.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **`Fixes #33238`: answered.** The live PR body opens `Part of #33238`, and no commit message carries a closing keyword, so the card stays open for the hot-upgrade path and the doors that do not announce.
- **ADR-0150 D7 addendum ("boot only"), the `PositionSchema.renamedFrom` describe text and the `packages/spec/liveness/position.json` line: still escalated.** The separate Tier H docs PR is owed with this change; the PR body names it seat-filed, which this review did not verify.
- **The runtime install and enable routes that do not announce, and the re-register finding: still the lane seat's**, as in round 1.
- **`security_findings: withheld`** in the patch report is consistent with round 1.

### ④ Design judgment

No `hits` file. Both implementing files were read against ruling A1 and against the announcers on `origin/main`. No must-fix and no should-fix.

Tried against the scoping and found sound: a payload with no `changed`, a non-array `changed`, non-string, empty or path-shaped entries and other item types name nothing; an `app/ID` whose package the registry does not hold names nothing; a `position/NAME` entry admits only claims whose new name is `NAME`; two packages in one announcement are each judged by the boot's rules; an old name with one claim in scope and one outside is refused `claimed-twice`, and nothing out of scope is carried; a package withdrawn between its announcement and its queued run has no claim left to judge; runner behaviour (boot gate, one promise chain, failures never thrown to the announcing door) is as in round 1.

**Nits (no effect on correctness or the contract):**

1. `position-renamed-holder-carry.ts` "When it runs" and the hook comment in `security-plugin-start-hooks.ts`: one announcer has a second payload shape the text does not name; the text should say that entries in the `app/ID` or `position/NAME` spelling count whichever announcer sends them. Detail held by review#2.
2. "When it runs" describes the admitted `position/NAME` and `app/NAME` entries more narrowly than the code admits (any grammar-valid position name; any `app/` name that is a held package id). Same judgement over registered claims; only the wording is narrower.

Both are jsdoc inside implementing files, so a fix moves the head: accepted deviations, or folded into the owed docs follow-up. Nits alone end the round.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-33238-position-rename-hot-install`
Reviewed-by: `session_01FEkQ5nhu4dRbKVQKDB4CDB`

**VERDICT: PASS**
